title: Offline AWQ/AWG/UI authority bridges and human gates
invariants: every operation is bound to the exact task revision, lease, session, and worktree
pending authority outcomes require explicit observation and cannot approve
timeout and unknown outcomes require an explicit bounded retry or remain blocked
AWQ acceptance is attributed to AWQ and cannot be produced by the runtime
required refinements, test changes, specification changes, and repair escalations require AWG routing followed by UI approval
rejection, timeout, unknown, stale, replayed, crossed, and ambiguous outcomes fail closed
resume preserves the original binding and operation fingerprint
limitations: The local fakes prove protocol behavior only and are not live AWQ, AWG, or UI clients.
A successful fixture proves authority attribution and fail-closed control flow, not quality, guidance, or human intent.
Runtime evidence contains digests and identifiers only; private authority content is intentionally absent.
